content.value_statement: Payment features fail when checkout, subscriptions, and webhooks are built without clear security controls. This skill guides secure processor integrations with practical validation, retry, and compliance checks.
actual_capabilities: Plans checkout flows for Stripe, PayPal, Square, and similar processors.
Guides webhook signature verification and idempotent event processing.
Outlines subscription billing, recurring payment, refund, and dispute handling.
Provides PCI-aware practices that avoid raw card data handling.
Defines test scenarios for failed payments, retries, and production migration.
limitations: Does not replace processor documentation or legal PCI compliance review.
Does not provide live credentials, merchant account setup, or production approval.
Requires the user to confirm the selected processor, framework, and deployment environment.
Cannot verify live payment behavior without access to test systems and logs.

use_cases.title: Launch a Checkout Flow
use_cases.description: Design a secure checkout flow that uses tokenized card collection, server-side validation, and clear payment states.

use_cases.title: Harden Webhook Processing
use_cases.description: Review webhook endpoints for signature verification, raw body handling, idempotency, and retry-safe processing.

use_cases.title: Plan Subscription Billing
use_cases.description: Map billing lifecycle events for trials, renewals, failed payments, cancellations, refunds, and disputes.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Payment Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new payment feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a payment flow for my app. Ask for the processor, product type, currencies, subscription needs, and compliance constraints before recommending an approach.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Checkout Safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate implementation of checkout and server validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secure checkout integration for [processor] in [framework]. Include client tokenization, server-side payment confirmation, error handling, and test scenarios.

prompt_templates.title: Review Webhook Security
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of asynchronous payment events.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this webhook design for [processor]. Check signature verification, raw body preservation, idempotency, queue handling, retries, and duplicate event protection.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Billing Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my payment architecture for production readiness. Cover checkout, subscriptions, refunds, disputes, logging, secrets, PCI scope, observability, and rollback plans.

output_examples.input: I need Stripe checkout for a SaaS subscription product.
output: A recommended checkout sequence using Stripe-hosted or tokenized card collection.
Server-side validation steps before activating the subscription.
Webhook events to handle for renewals, payment failures, and cancellations.
Test cases for trial conversion, failed renewal, refund, and duplicate webhook delivery.

output_examples.input: Review my PayPal webhook plan before launch.
output: A checklist for signature verification and raw body handling.
Idempotency guidance using stored event identifiers.
Recommendations for fast acknowledgements and queued background processing.
Failure scenarios covering retries, out-of-order events, and provider API confirmation.

output_examples.input: Prepare a PCI-aware payment implementation checklist.
output: Use provider-hosted fields or approved tokenization components.
Keep raw card data out of application logs, databases, and servers.
Separate test and production credentials with deployment checks.
Validate payment state on the server before granting access.

best_practices: Use official SDKs and tokenized payment components for card collection.
Verify webhooks with raw request bodies before processing any event.
Store idempotency keys and provider event IDs for every payment operation.
anti_patterns: Do not store, log, or transmit raw card numbers through your application.
Do not trust client payment responses without server-side provider validation.
Do not process webhooks before signature verification and duplicate checks.

faq.question: Which payment processors does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on Stripe, PayPal, Square, and similar processors that support checkout, subscriptions, and webhooks.

faq.question: Can this skill make my application PCI compliant?
faq.answer: No. It gives PCI-aware engineering guidance, but formal compliance needs processor documentation, business review, and qualified assessment when required.

faq.question: Does it handle webhook security?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes signature verification, raw body preservation, idempotency, duplicate protection, and server-side provider checks.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready payment code?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation patterns, but production code still needs local testing, processor test mode validation, and security review.

faq.question: Does it support subscription billing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers trials, renewals, cancellations, failed payments, refunds, disputes, and lifecycle webhook events.

faq.question: What information should I provide before using it?
faq.answer: Provide the processor, framework, product type, billing model, countries, currencies, and deployment environment.
